news.title: Ghana clear major hurdle in bid to end 20-year World Cup absence
news.lede: Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens. Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens, showed great courage to come from behind and defeat Côte d'Ivoire 2-1 in Casablanca. This victory keeps their dream of playing in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup alive. The match started badly for Ghana.

news.title: India football ‘closer than ever’ to overseas players representing the nation
news.lede: Dubai: A major development for Indian football is on the horizon, with the country’s football authorities increasingly confident that players of Indian heritage based in Europe could soon be eligible to represent the national team.. Current rules bar Indian-heritage footballers based overseas from representing the national team unless they give up their foreign passport.. The rules have so far denied Indian footballers living abroad the chance to earn international caps and help the country climb back into the FIFA top 100.. However, one senior official told Sky Sports News he is “convinced” the way will soon be cleared for eligible overseas-based players to represent India..

news.title: Oceania declares support for Infantino in boost for Fifa president but New Zealand breaks ranks
news.lede: OFC’s 11 votes could prove crucial in Fifa election. Stance shows continued backing from smaller nations. The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) has declared its support for Gianni Infantino following demands from Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation for the Fifa president to resign, in a development that further highlights world football’s civil war. After a meeting of its executive committee in Fiji on Wednesday, the OFC issued a statement on Friday praising “the progress achieved over the last decade” by Fifa in its first public comments since the abandoned World Cup sell-off plan emerged this month.

news.title: Key Arab Football Federations Reaffirm Support For FIFA President Infantino
news.lede: Amidst a growing global football governance crisis, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has secured crucial backing from six Arab federations, including World Cup hosts Morocco and Qatar, even as European and Oceania bodies withdraw support over his controversial private investment plan. The heads of six Arab soccer federations expressed their "full support" and "confidence" in Gianni Infantino on Thursday as the embattled FIFA president fights to keep his job after his failed World Cup private investment plan. The backing came from 2030 World Cup co-host Morocco, Qatar, Egypt, Mauritania, Lebanon and Sudan, with four of the signatories being FIFA council members.
